sphere_commentary.overview:
The three series show comparable central tendencies, with HEALING and THRIVING near 7.0 and TRANSFORMING slightly lower at 6.6.
• HEALING has the largest sample (n=574) and the most consistent responses across its 12 protocols.
• THRIVING records the highest single‑protocol score (T‑FC‑L3 7.63) and a mean similar to HEALING, indicating a robust efficacy floor.
• TRANSFORMING exhibits the greatest variability (SD 1.87) and the lowest protocol mean (X‑MC‑L3 5.7), matching its design for low‑affect states.
sphere_commentary.cross_series:
Each series behaves as designed: DESCENT drives regulation, HOLD sustains optimal states, and ASCENT enables gradual lift.
• HEALING DESCENT protocols cluster tightly (6.35–7.22) with fast settle times and high “balanced/comfortable” rhythm ratings.
• THRIVING HOLD protocols show a spread (6.46–7.63); Focus & Clarity L3 leads, while Creative Flow L3 also performs well, suggesting tiered dosing works.
• TRANSFORMING ASCENT/DESCENT mix yields the widest spread; X‑MD‑L3 matches HEALING sleep efficacy, hinting at cross‑zone resonance.
sphere_commentary.anomalies:
Several protocols show distributions or outcomes that merit closer inspection.
• X‑MC‑L3: very low mean (5.7) with high spread (SD 2.45) and sparse responses suggest possible population mismatch.
• T‑FC‑L3: bimodal distribution with a strong peak at score 10 alongside a 6‑8 cluster, indicating a responder subgroup experiencing ceiling effects.
• H‑CR‑L1: qualitative reports of “significant improvement” contrast with a modest mean (6.35), implying the 0‑10 scale may compress relief in acute distress.
• X‑MD‑L1: low mean (6.36) despite reports of balanced rhythm and quick settle, raising the question of readiness or activation energy needed.
• X‑MD‑L3: unexpectedly high mean (7.15) relative to L1/L2, suggesting the L3 variant may hit a different entrainment sweet spot.
sphere_commentary.development_signals:
Based on convergent patterns, the following concrete steps could refine the protocol set.
• X‑MC‑L3: investigate whether the DESCENT arc is appropriate for Mind & Clarity or test an ASCENT/HOLD variant; consider adding an HOLD phase.
• T‑FC‑L3: create an L4 variant with extended HOLD duration to test whether the ceiling effect at score 10 generalizes to a longer exposure.
• X‑MD‑L1: add Adviser routing logic to screen for readiness (e.g., low activation energy) before assigning this motivational protocol.
• H‑CR‑L1: trial a distress‑anchored response scale (e.g., 0‑5 where any relief scores higher) to better capture qualitative gains in crisis states.
• T‑MB‑L3: examine the HOLD architecture for a subset that reports “did not settled”; shorten or modulate the hold to reduce agitation.
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis:
Across runs, the analytical framing of many protocols has shifted, revealing both stable clusters and distinct outliers.
• CROSS‑RUN DRIFT: most protocols show similarity < 0.85 between earliest and latest runs, with X‑MD‑L3 (0.507), H‑SL‑L1 (0.530) and T‑FC‑L3 (0.532) exhibiting the strongest drift.
• CROSS‑PROTOCOL SEMANTIC CLUSTERS: tight pairings appear within families (T‑FC‑L1↔T‑FC‑L2 0.878, H‑SL‑L1↔H‑SL‑L2 0.869, T‑CF‑L1↔T‑CF‑L2 0.841), while H‑OS‑L3, T‑FC‑L3 and T‑CF‑L3 are the most analytically distinct (mean similarity ≈ 0.68–0.69).
• Confidence in these drift observations is moderate; the growing sample size likely drives genuine evolution rather than pure noise.

by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L1: Listeners felt noticeably calmer, with most reporting better sleep and steady breathing after use.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L2: Most people experienced reduced anxiety, though a few felt the effect was weaker or slower.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L3: Many reported a deep sense of calm, especially when used during stressful moments or caregiving.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L1: Even in high distress, users often felt relief, though the numeric score didn’t always capture how much they improved.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L2: People in crisis usually felt calmer after a few minutes, with music and rhythm rated as soothing.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L3: Some users felt immediate relief, while others needed a bit longer; opinions on the sound varied.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L1: Overstimulated listeners tended to feel steadier and more grounded after listening.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L2: Those overwhelmed by sensory input generally felt more settled, though a few found the music less engaging.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L3: Many users felt calmer and some used it to help with sleep, though reactions to the rhythm were mixed.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L1: Listeners commonly found it easier to fall asleep, with the music felt pleasant and the rhythm soothing.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L2: The protocol worked well in clinical or caregiving settings, though a few felt the rhythm was a bit busy.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L3: Most people reported settling quickly and feeling ready for rest, with the rhythm described as calm.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L1: Users felt a mild boost in creative flow, with some noticing the effect right away and others after a few minutes.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L2: Many reported a clear improvement in focus for creative work, with the music highly praised.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L3: Most felt a strong lift in creative concentration, with some describing the effect as powerful.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L1: People experienced better focus, though some noted the rhythm felt a little busy at times.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L2: Listeners generally felt sharper and more attentive, with the music well received.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L3: The majority felt significantly more focused, with the music liked or loved and the rhythm steady.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L1: Users felt more balanced in energy and mood, with the music neutral or liked and the rhythm smooth.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L2: Most experienced steady energy, though a few found the rhythm slightly uneven or busy.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L3: Many felt balanced, but a small group said they didn’t settle at all; the rest liked the music and rhythm.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L1: Listeners usually felt clearer in thought, though a couple said it made things feel worse.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L2: Most felt their thinking was sharper, with the music enjoyed and the rhythm described as very settling.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L3: Responses were mixed: some felt a little better, some felt no change, and a few felt worse.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L1: People low on motivation often felt a gentle nudge forward, though the effect varied.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L2: Those feeling lethargic usually felt a bit more energy, though the change was modest.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L3: A surprising number felt a clear lift in mood and energy, despite the low scores for the other levels.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L1: Listeners with low mood or energy often felt a steady lift, with the music neutral or liked and the rhythm smooth.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L2: Many felt their mood improve, especially when trying to sleep or during therapy, with the music well liked.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L3: Most felt a modest improvement in energy, with some reporting no change and the music generally liked.
